entities.summary: Agustín Leonardo was a Spanish painter of the Baroque period, born in Tarazona, Aragon, in 1580, and died in 1640. He was trained by the renowned painter Francisco de Zurbarán and later collaborated with Diego Velázquez, leading to the creation of some of the most iconic works of the era. Leonardo's style blended realism and drama, as seen in his frescoes in the Royal Palace of Madrid, which he painted with Velázquez. The duo's artistic partnership had a lasting impact on Spanish art, influencing subsequent generations of painters. Leonardo's work continues to be celebrated for its technical skill and emotional depth, making him one of the most important artists of the Baroque period. His legacy can be seen in the many museums and galleries that showcase his works, including the Prado Museum in Madrid, which holds an extensive collection of his paintings.
